notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check with no warning on any gate (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: the R2 hardware backend is refused by the loader until reviewed_by is set in driver.lock.json. The package covers one entry symbol of the card, elliptec.shutter:Shutter (an ELL6 dual-position slider used as an optical shutter): three reads (is_open, is_closed, slot), cap.optics.shutter.v1 for open/close, and three extension actions (home, move to slot 1/2, close as the safe-state action). NOT COVERED: the other four entry symbols of the card (elliptec.iris:Iris, elliptec.linear:Linear, elliptec.rotator:Rotator, elliptec.slider:Slider) are separate devices served by the same library and are not exposed here; one package per repository is the rule. NOT COVERED: Shutter.jog and the relative/absolute moves of Shutter.move, and the motor settings (jog step, home offset, bus address, motor frequencies) - the clone documents the jog step only as a get/set pair on the device, not as a distance the driver could bound. NOT COVERED: whether the mount was built inverted is a hardware-factory option (native.py inverted=), so the driver reports the raw slot and the open/closed state of the object; it names close as the safe state because closing blocks the beam. The hardware backend (native.py, a real serial port) was never run, and the fake is an in-memory slider, not a recording of the device. gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
